name: Hereditary spastic paraplegia SPG11 (thin corpus callosum)

reference.source: GeneReviews / Bradley's Neurology in Clinical Practice
clinicalPearls: SPG11, caused by biallelic variants in SPG11 encoding spatacsin, is the commonest autosomal recessive complicated HSP and the classic cause of HSP with a thin corpus callosum
Onset is usually in childhood or adolescence with progressive spastic paraparesis accompanied by cognitive impairment or learning difficulty
A peripheral neuropathy is frequently present, producing distal wasting and areflexia that can coexist with the pyramidal signs
Brain MRI characteristically shows a thin corpus callosum, often with periventricular white-matter changes and the 'ears of the lynx' sign on FLAIR
Additional features may include cerebellar signs, parkinsonism, and a progressive maculopathy
The combination of early cognitive decline, thin corpus callosum, and spasticity distinguishes SPG11 from pure dominant forms such as SPG4
Care is multidisciplinary and symptomatic, covering spasticity, cognition, mobility, and bladder function
reference.pathophysiology: As with other hereditary spastic paraplegias, the primary event is length-dependent degeneration of the longest corticospinal axons. SPG11 encodes spatacsin, a protein involved in autophagic lysosome reformation and intracellular trafficking. Loss of function leads to accumulation of autophagic and lysosomal material and impaired membrane trafficking within neurones. The resulting neurodegeneration is more widespread than in pure HSP, affecting corticospinal tracts, the corpus callosum and cerebral white matter, peripheral nerves, and other regions, which accounts for the complicated, multisystem neurological phenotype.
additionalDifferentials: Other complicated hereditary spastic paraplegias (e.g. SPG15, SPG7)
Metabolic and lysosomal storage disorders with spasticity and cognitive decline
Early-onset neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to identify a thin corpus callosum, white-matter change, and the 'ears of the lynx' sign
Genetic testing for SPG11 within a comprehensive HSP panel, including deletion/duplication analysis
Nerve conduction studies and EMG to characterise the associated peripheral neuropathy
Neuropsychological assessment to document and monitor cognitive impairment
Metabolic screening to exclude treatable storage or leukodystrophy mimics
redFlags: Rapidly progressive cognitive or motor decline suggesting an alternative degenerative or metabolic disorder
Prominent bulbar involvement or fasciculations raising concern for juvenile motor neurone disease
New focal deficit or seizures prompting reassessment and imaging
Visual loss from maculopathy requiring ophthalmological review
reference.prognosis: SPG11 is progressive, and most affected individuals lose independent ambulation within one to two decades of onset, with accumulating cognitive impairment; life expectancy may be reduced in advanced disease although the course varies.
pitfalls: Overlooking the coexisting peripheral neuropathy and attributing all signs to the pyramidal lesion
Missing the thin corpus callosum by not reviewing midline MRI sequences
Assuming pure HSP and not testing for recessive complicated forms in early-onset cases with cognitive decline
Failing to arrange multidisciplinary support for cognitive and educational needs
management: Treat spasticity symptomatically with antispasticity agents such as baclofen or tizanidine, botulinum toxin and intrathecal baclofen, alongside physiotherapy and mobility aids
Provide occupational therapy and wheelchairs or assistive devices as independent ambulation is progressively lost
Manage the associated peripheral neuropathy and supply orthoses for distal weakness and deformity
Offer neuropsychological support and cognitive or educational rehabilitation for the progressive cognitive impairment
Monitor for and manage additional features such as parkinsonism, cerebellar signs and maculopathy
Deliver care through a multidisciplinary neurorehabilitation team
Offer genetic counselling for autosomal recessive SPG11 inheritance with family testing
